vanishing world by sayaka murata.

scenes that stood out to me:
- when amane's husband saku was giving birth and the doctor had to basically flipped open his artificial skin?? that was apparently hanging from his stomach to above his knees. like imagine the growth of this skin and the baby is hella visible when he is naked. this scene made me gaped on the train when i read it. intense but also disgusting and creepy. 

- the last few pages of amane basically raping one of the kodommo-chans. this is true insanity right here, someone lock this woman up. amane also imprisoned her own mom??? i feel the mother kinda didnt deserve. to be fair she did impose her ideals of sex on amane and that made her second think her whole life, and changed the way she view and behave in romantic relationships but i also think she suffered tremendously since her husband left her and amane alone. im also curious on how they decided to get to that point to commit "incest" in the story. these horny bastards.

- the whole idea of how husband and wife is just a title but symbolically, the relationships is more like a sibling. which is crazy and surreal? oh wait i think its because every child is an individual, like there are no siblings. but why do you have to marry a stranger though. the way love is depicted in this story is very superficial, no one genuinely loves another because everything is just an act, to comply and conform to society ideals. WHICH i think is kind of relatable in singapore context especially with the "if you want to own a house early, you have to get married or start a family" etc. as i am typing now, i think im slowly figuring out the main themes of this book. yay me.

- there are only very few scenes of amane and her friendships. there was a scene with one of her female friends, cant remember her name i think its juni or something, but she basically reacted so brutally honest to amane when she mentioned she commit adutery stuff with her plushies and characters, to satisfy her own pleasure. and juni did not like that, but she was one of the firsts to start a family with her husband. and i dont think she ever had a boyfriend? like she just becomes a mom and then that was it. i think there was definitely more to be explored with her character.

- amane was dining with one of her female colleagues and she said pleasuring yourself with characters is like raping them lmao. amane was taken aback but she got her pov. i think this idea could also be relevant to current times because people look up to fandom and stuff, not for pleasure (at least i don think most do) but by what makes them characters that they find relatable, and naturally they would deem them as something sacred, untouchable, on a higher level. so when some troll comes in and say shit about their characters they start throwing hands, which becomes fandom wars or pure internet hate. so i think the invention of amane's colleague is probably for this group of people.

scenes that stood out to me:

- when ken did not die after fighting two demonic ass looking wolves.

james by percival everett

this story is bout to go down in history for the next century as one of the most living and real look into being black in a time of slavery. my heart hurts for them. no one should ever go through what they went through, its so inhumane.

scenes that stood out to me:
- jim/james joined the choir, with emile and norman and the other guys who were white but were pretending to be black performers just for gags and laughs. this was some crazy shit. i thought emile was going to turn out to be the good guy but just like the rest of the white, he was a waste of space because he started treating jim badly :( he did not beat him up physically but it still fecks with your psyche. the way he still bought him with his money, jim was still a slave even though he was not exactly physically shackled or harmed, he still had to perform like 200 times to pay off the debt. 

- the way james is always so courageous to run away, his bravery really speaks through the story. this man is willing to take as many chances to escape and take his life under his hands, by learning to read and write.

- when james revealed he is huck's father i was like WTF??? did not see that coming at all. but i did not like how it was revealed because it makes the book seem cheap, it kinda make it seem like james was doing all that not because huck was huck but because they were blood related. it watered down the significance of their relationship i feel. also i dont really know where huck went? he got saved fom drowning after the ship broke in half, i think he might have went to fought the war???

- the rape scene of tom hopkins, raping the black woman who was proving solace to james with her husband, when he came back running to hannibal, after knowing his wife and daughter was sold and gone. this hopkins guy deserved his death honestly, that was brutal. and it was the way only a few words and sentences was enough to paint the whole picture of how these white people committing these crimes could always get away so easily after taking advantage of a black woman's agency and existence. hate these men. also did not know he was the tom friend huck kept talking about until james went to "visit" judge thatcher, the guy who bought him initially, making his life hell.

- when james was teaching his kids on how to speak the black language. it was a funny scene but it's still a very sad reality. because they have to pretend to be dumb, illiterate, and powerless when they for sure can outwin these cowards by a mile and more. it really hurts to know that this was the reality for the black community for so many decades back then. 

- the adventures with huck was a nice read, and good break from all the suffering, and beatings the innocents have to experience just because of the colour of their skin. i hate racist people. 

really glad i watched d'angelo wallace's video on his book recommendations, without watching it i wouldn't have discovered such a well written and virtuoso book at the ripe age of 25.
